newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds outperform U.S. on rate hopes.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds outperform U.S. on rate hopes.

text.p: Australian bonds ended a six day run of underperformance against U.S. debt as the local market firmed in anticipation of a domestic interest rate cut being announced later this week.

The Reserve Bank board meets on Tuesday, and the bank is widely expected to announce a cut in 7.0 percent official interest rates on Wednesday following a string of data suggesting the economy remains sluggish.

The firm tone was in the face of a weakened U.S. market, which took profits ahead of this week's Presidential election and quarterly refunding auctions, and saw the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread back below 100 basis points.

However, the local market still has some way to go before it gets back to the low-80s seen just after the benign quarterly inflation report two weeks ago, and one of the key factors which has led the market to believe a rate cut is in the offing.
There was no trading in U.S. Treasuries in Tokyo on Monday due to a holiday in Japan.
Meanwhile, the market continued to lag Canadian bonds, which themselves are pricing in a further easing by the Bank of Canada due to a strengthening Canadian dollar.
New Zealand debt closed little changed from Friday's closing levels. -- Colin Brinsden 61-2 9373-1800
